---
title: "Manuscript title here"
# The short title, or running head, some journals ask for: printed as
# "Short title: ..." under the title of every document -- in the title's
# font and size in the .docx, a size smaller in the .pdf and the .html.
# Leave it out and nothing is printed.
# short-title: "Short title here"
# The authors, in order, each with the ids of their affiliations: the
# numbers are worked out from here, in the order the authors name them, and
# written on one line with the names in every render. The corresponding
# author carries `corresponding: true` and an `email:`. Each affiliation is
# one line, `address:`, written as the paper prints it. It can also go in
# place, quoted: `affiliations: ["University X, City, Country"]`.
# Each author's ORCID iD goes in `orcid:`: it puts the ORCID icon, linked to
# the record, beside the name in the README, and reaches the metadata of the
# data and the Zenodo deposit.
# The copyright holders in LICENSE-CODE.txt and in the README come from this
# block.
author:
  - name: Author1
    affiliations: [aff1]
    orcid:            # the ORCID iD: XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX
    email: correspondent@example.org
    corresponding: true
  - name: Author2
    affiliations: [aff2]
    orcid:            # the ORCID iD: XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX
affiliations:
  - id: aff1
    address: Institution 1, Department, City, Country
  - id: aff2
    address: Institution 2, Department, City, Country
# The journal this manuscript is going to: a .csl in references/. Every
# command reads it from here, so you name it once. list_journals() shows what
# you have, and add_journal("ecology-letters") fetches another. Naming one in
# a call -- render_docx("ecology-letters") -- wins for that call alone.
csl: references/journal-of-ecology.csl
# No date: a manuscript is dated by the journal, not by the day you happened
# to render it, and a date on a draft you circulate only ever misleads. Add
# `date: today` and `date-format: long` back here if you want one; a blinded
# main text drops it either way.
---

```{r affiliations}
#| include: true
#| echo: false
#| purl: false
# The affiliations and the correspondence line, numbered from the YAML above.
# A double-blind submission leaves this chunk out; the title page is given it.
easypaper::affiliations()
```

```{r package-bibliography}
#| include: false
#| purl: false
# Writes the .bib entries of the packages in use, so they can be cited in
# Methods. It runs last, once they are all loaded. Pandoc reads packages.bib
# after knitr, so citations already work in this same pass.
#
# .packages() only sees what is ATTACHED during the render. Packages that
# prepared the data or the metadata (dataspice, readxl) ran in another session
# and would never get an entry, yet they deserve the citation as much as the
# rest. They are added by name; any that is not installed is skipped.
#
# write_packages_bib() is knitr::write_bib() with the names in the titles
# kept as written -- {vegan}, {Quarto} -- whatever case the journal's style
# sets titles in.
pkg_extra <- c("knitr", "quarto", "rmarkdown", "renv", "dataspice", "readxl",
               "easypaper")
pkg_extra <- pkg_extra[vapply(pkg_extra, requireNamespace, logical(1),
                              quietly = TRUE)]
easypaper::write_packages_bib(c(.packages(), pkg_extra),
                              here::here("references/packages.bib"))
```
